findings.statement: REQ-LG-004 defines the tail a commit was built on by two values, `seq` = `base` and commit hash = `prev`, 'so the appended commit keeps the hash chain (LG-C04)'. It also says the writer 'SHALL append it only after the `seq` of its `base`; when the ledger has moved since it was opened, the writer reads it again and checks the commit against it'. In REQ-CL-004 the command runs that check only 'When the store answers that the tail moved', and the `store` port stays unchanged (proposal.md Impact; `append(commit, after: number)` compares `seq` only). Suppose the tail is replaced at the same `seq` between opening and appending, for example by a git checkout or rebase of `store/knowledge.jsonl` onto another branch's ledger, or by a hand edit. The store does not answer `moved`, the commit is appended, and the chain breaks. The next opening then refuses the ledger with LG-C04, code 2. So 'moved' means a `seq` change for the writer and a `seq` or hash change for the check. Design D-6 says 'a tail replaced at the same `seq` cannot pass and break the chain'. That holds for the pure `checkTail`, not for the command. I-12 closes review 2 F-6 only at the level of the pure check.
findings.recommendation: Say in REQ-LG-004 or REQ-CL-004 that the writer learns that the tail moved only from the store's `moved` answer, which compares `seq`. Say that until the store adapters of #57 (LG-C06), a tail rewritten at the same `seq` is not caught at append and is refused by LG-C04 at the next opening. Narrow the claim in D-6 to `checkTail`.

findings.statement: proposal.md, What Changes, 'Tail (LG-C03)': 'a commit whose `base` is not the tail of the ledger when it is appended is rejected with rule `LG-C03`'. REQ-LG-004, after I-6 and I-12, answers `existing` and not LG-C03 when the moved ledger already holds the commit's `proposal`. SCN-CL-014 and the third case of SCN-LG-005 pin that answer, exit 0 with `{"outcome":"commit","seq":1}`. REQ-LG-004 also rejects a tail whose `seq` matches but whose hash is not the commit's `prev`. The bullet says the opposite of the spec for two writers of one proposal and leaves out the hash.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the Tail bullet: 'a commit whose `base` and `prev` are not the `seq` and hash of the tail when it is appended is rejected with rule `LG-C03` instead of being refused with code 2, unless the ledger already holds a commit of the same proposal, which is then answered (LG-C08)'.

findings.statement: I-4 added two obligations to REQ-AR-011. First, 'a fixture whose ledger does not open fails the test, naming the folder', where the ledger is `ledger.jsonl`, or `ledger.jsonl` followed by `moved.jsonl`. Second, `expected.json` holds at least one rejection. SCN-AR-017, the only scenario of the requirement, still exercises only a missing folder and an extra folder. A test carrying the token SCN-AR-017 can omit both new failure modes and still satisfy the scenario, so these clauses have no verifying scenario. tasks.md 3.2 lists them, but the spec does not pin them.
findings.recommendation: Extend SCN-AR-017. WHEN: the test also runs with a fixture folder whose `ledger.jsonl` followed by `moved.jsonl` does not open, and with a fixture folder whose `expected.json` is `[]`. THEN: each is reported with the name of its folder.

findings.statement: SCN-LG-003 reads: 'apply runs on a proposal of a new session event and the four entity intents …; then on the same proposal with the body of `lattice/fx-a02` changed; then on the same proposal with the type of `lattice/fx-a01` changed to `lattice/table.rule@2`'. In the third case, 'the same proposal' can mean the one just modified, with fx-a02 changed. On that reading the commit holds fx-a01, fx-a02 and the session event. The THEN clause, 'records are `lattice/fx-a01` at `rev` 2 … and the session event', fits only the first proposal. REQ-LG-005 and design D-7 build 'each proposal of SCN-LG-003' from this text. This is the same pattern as review 1 F-9, which was fixed in SCN-LG-001.
findings.recommendation: Write 'then on the first proposal with …' in the second and third cases, or name the proposals (P1…P4) and refer to them by name in SCN-LG-004 ('the second proposal of SCN-LG-003').

proposals.change: REQ-LG-004: say that the writer learns that the tail moved from the store's `moved` answer, which compares `seq`, and that a tail rewritten at the same `seq` is caught by LG-C04 at the next opening until #57 (F-1). SCN-LG-003: 'then on the first proposal with …' in its second and third cases (F-4).
Tail bullet: name `prev` as well as `base`, and add the `existing` answer for a ledger that already holds a commit of the same proposal (F-2).
SCN-AR-017: add a fixture folder whose ledger does not open and one whose `expected.json` is empty, each reported with its folder name (F-3).
D-6: limit 'a tail replaced at the same `seq` cannot pass and break the chain' to the pure `checkTail`. The command sees only the store's `moved` answer, which compares `seq` (F-1).

assumptions.statement: I read issue #56 from the scratchpad copy i56.md (typed checks moved to #82) and the review 1 and 2 envelopes from the scratchpad. The guard of the review Run allows no shell command except `warrant run submit`, so I did not use `gh`.

Sources the spec must agree with: design-next/03-ledger.md (LG-C02, LG-C03, LG-C05, LG-C07, LG-C08, LG-P01, LG-P04, LG-P05, LG-A02, LG-A03) and 02-object-model.md (OM-E01, OM-H01, OM-H03). Baseline of the MODIFIED requirements: the merged openspec/specs/{cli,architecture}. I checked the current code (src/ledger/**, src/assembly/index.ts, src/adapters/store-jsonl, test/architecture/rules.test.ts, test/cli/apply.test.ts, test/fixtures/rules/**) only as context.

The closures of review 2 hold. I-8: REQ-LG-003 item 1 and REQ-CL-004 `existing` state the limit. I worked through SCN-LG-004 by hand. The re-run on the ledger holding seq 2 has held intents {fx-a02, S2} and answers `existing` with seq 2. After fx-a01 is written at rev 2, the held intents are {fx-a01, fx-a02, S2} and the answer is LG-P02 for exactly those two ids. I-9: a proposal file already gone counts as removed, and SCN-CL-014 covers it. I-10: proposal.md No-op and Re-apply, and REQ-LG-001's split between the proposal hash and the commit's `proposal`. I-11: 'Unless it answers `existing`' in REQ-LG-002. I-12: `{seq, hash}` in REQ-LG-002 and REQ-LG-004, SCN-LG-005 and SCN-CL-011; it is closed for the pure check, and the residual gap at the command level is F-1. I-13: the type-change case in SCN-LG-003; its wording is F-4.

I checked by hand the paths and counts in SCN-LG-001, SCN-LG-002, SCN-CL-007 and SCN-CL-011 against the canonical order of the fixture proposal: fixture, fx-a01, fx-a02, fx-a03, session. I also checked that LG-C07, LG-P01 and LG-P02 rejections with the `/intents/<i>` prefix stripped do not change under permutation, duplicates of three or more intents and no-op duplicates included. I found no defect there.
